entries.claim: Output shaping defaults to --shape-output auto on a metered session and is ON only when all three hold: the paired decision-equivalence verdict is at or above the shared reporting floor (50 A/B + 30 A/A), its harm bound (lower end of the paired difference interval) is inside the pre-registered +/-2pp certification margin, and the shadow output-token delta excludes zero on the saving side over at least 50 priced samples. Otherwise OFF with a stated reason. Turn-on evidence comes only from shadow rows tagged levers.shape == off, so shaped rows cannot keep shaping on; shaped rows at or above the floor whose harm bound is outside the budget turn it off; both sets are read over the last 7 days. Always off on subscription/OAuth. The last published live sample (398 A/B, 399 A/A) predates the lever tag and counts as zero rows; its harm bound (-4.5pp) is outside the 2pp budget regardless, so auto resolves to OFF.
entries.note: Mechanism is resolve_shape_output; the live-sample figures are from benchmarks/results/shadow-live-2026-09-15.json. The rule is covered by the decision matrix in tests/test_output.py; the thresholds are read from shadow.VERDICT_MIN_AB/VERDICT_MIN_AA and certify.gate.CERT_MARGIN (via output.SHAPE_HARM_MARGIN), not re-declared. Reply LENGTH cannot be measured offline (the deterministic oracle decides from blocks and emits no prose), so there is no corpus number for shaping and none is claimed: the n=6 output_pairs.jsonl A/B is a hand-written mechanism check, already labelled illustrative on the page. The README paragraph in the savings section restates this entry and originates no fact of its own.

entries.claim: On the maintainer's own Claude Code traffic (13,191 priced requests, 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-24, all in digest mode), distil saved an estimated 10.2% of the counterfactual bill: $286 saved against $2,510 billed, with cache reads and writes priced at list rates.
entries.note: realized.saved_share_of_counterfactual_bill = 0.1024, realized.saved_usd_estimated = 286.26, billed_usd_total = 2510.45, requests_priced = 13191. One machine, one user, one mode: it is a real bill, not a population estimate, and every surface that quotes it says whose traffic it is. 'Estimated' because tokens saved are rescaled to billed scale and priced at each request's own blended input rate (the artifact's realized.note). Regenerate with benchmarks/live_savings_decomposition.py --since 2026-09-01. Gross of distil's own overhead: the headline now quotes it together with the netted range in v-live-bill-net-of-overhead.

entries.claim: The 10.2% live saving was measured before distil's own spend was netted out: expand re-queries (0.07–0.34 pp) and shadow replays (at least 0.92 pp, about 1.6 pp scaled to every row) were not in the ledger. Net of them the corrected estimate is about 9%, 8.3–9.2% of the same counterfactual bill, still before the replays' own cache reads and writes.
entries.note: Arithmetic in the artifact's 'Net of the overhead' section: ($286.26 − $1.93 − $25.80) / $2,796.71 = 9.2% and ($286.26 − $9.54 − $45.12) / $2,796.71 = 8.3%. An estimate, not a measurement: 0 of the 13,191 rows carry the new upstream_calls / expand_requery_usage fields. A re-run of benchmarks/live_savings_decomposition.py on a window recorded after the accounting fix replaces it with a measured figure.

entries.claim: Pre-registered live run of distil mcp on claude-haiku-4-5 (2026-09-25, protocol v1 + Amendment 1): n=1000 tool tasks per level, n=630 result tasks. Right tool 94.4% raw vs 95.2% / 95.4% / 99.8% / 98.8% (L0-L3); right tool and arguments 91.2% raw vs 92.1% / 95.4% / 96.3% / 95.4%; R answer accuracy 99.7% raw vs 99.5%. Every level and R certified non-inferior (TOST + paired bootstrap, margin 0.02, alpha 0.05). Billed on the tool suite: raw $2.17, L0 $2.00, L1 $1.90, L2 $8.79, L3 $1.82; result suite raw $3.08, R $1.92; total $21.68 of an $85 ceiling. One model, eight reference servers, synthetic single-call tasks; no replication model.

entries.snippet: a true 20% saving at the shipped rate and log-sd 1.0 was detected
entries.claim: Known-answer Monte Carlo for distil ab at the shipped settings: false-alarm rate of the capped empirical-Bernstein headline under 20 looks is 0.0% at every tail weight (log-sd 0.6-2.0) and holdout (5%, 50%), against up to 10.5% for the normal-mixture mSPRT it replaced (4.0/6.5/10.5/10.5% at a 5% holdout; 2.0/2.5/1.0/0.5% at 50%); power for a true 20% saving at a 5% holdout and log-sd 1.0 is 1.5% at 4,000 sessions and 76% at 20,000; with distil 10% dearer per session and 25% more re-asks the headline reads +9.2% while cost per task reads about -12%; a model change adding 40% turns in both arms reads as 40% more cost before/after; CUPED cuts the efficient estimate's variance 44%.

entries.claim: Real tau-bench traffic, 100 decision points (60 held out, 4 reps), certifier candidates paired against claude-opus-4-8 on the deployed metric equiv_expand_act (next action unchanged by compression with distil_expand recovery), held-out cases. Next action kept with recovery: claude-opus-4-8 90.8%, claude-opus-5-5 90.8%, claude-opus-5-5 at low 90.0%, claude-sonnet-5-5 at low 94.6%, claude-haiku-4-5 85.0%. Paired change (points) and its 95% lower bound: opus-5-5 +0.0 / -10.0, opus-5-5 low -0.8 / -9.8, sonnet-5-5 low +3.8 / -4.5, haiku-4-5 -5.8 / -15.8. Distil digests alone without recovery: 61.3%, 73.3%, 75.0%, 66.7%, 44.2%. Two full calls agree: 92.5%, 93.3%, 94.2%, 99.2%, 96.7%. Truncation control diverges: 89.2%, 73.3%, 75.8%, 79.6%, 93.3%. Cost per case: $0.1458, $0.1336, $0.1256, $0.0619, $0.0248; claude-sonnet-5-5 at low is 57.5% cheaper than claude-opus-4-8. The pre-registered gates were a quality lower bound of at least -5 points, self-consistency no worse, truncation control at least 0.8× the incumbent's, at least 15% cheaper, and the mechanism explained; sonnet-5-5 at low passed all five. The deployed default certifier since 1.56.0 is claude-sonnet-5-5 at effort=low.
entries.note: Recomputed from the per-case rows by benchmarks/model_migration_summary.py (paired over held-out cases, each case averaged over its reps, 95% CI from the case-level differences). Live model calls were made once; the page restates the committed summary and does not re-run them. Reproduce the rows: python benchmarks/model_migration_eval.py (see model-migration.html#rerun). The 57.5% is headline.cost_reduction (1 - 0.0619/0.1458); the gate thresholds (-5 points, 0.8x, 15%) are the pre-registered rule, not measurements, and are restated from docs/adr/0020-default-live-certifier.md. The page's 'mechanism' gate is reported as passed per the eval record; its supporting trace analysis is not in summary.json.

This is an open decision-level risk on one model and one small set, not a task-success result: the SWE-bench outcome eval (v-swebench-outcome-300) is the task-level check.
